title: Created weak
hookLine: Allah wants to lighten your burden, for humans were created weak (4:28)
tomorrow: The near neighbor and the far

lines: A PAUSE IN THE FAMILY LAW.
cards: Some people open scripture expecting to be measured and found short: a list of rules, a standard nobody meets, a voice disappointed in them.

Then, in the middle of family law in an-Nisa, after rules about whom you may marry and what to do if you can't afford it, the Qur'an pauses and says something about the reader that sounds almost tender.
It explains why the rules are shaped the way they are. Because of what people are.

teach.h: TO MAKE CLEAR, TO GUIDE, TO TURN
teach.b: Read verses 26 to 28 together. God wants to make things clear to you, guide you in the ways of those before you, and turn to you in mercy, while those who follow their desires want you to swerve far off.
Then 4:28, in Pickthall's words: "Allah would make the burden light for you, for man was created weak." Khuliqa al-insanu da'ifa. Da'if means weak, frail.
Notice what the verse doesn't say. Not that people chose weakness, or that it's a failure. They were created that way.
Weakness is part of the design, and the law is built around it. Commentators gave examples: weak in the face of desire, in patience, in body.

In context, the marriage rules just before include allowances for people who can't manage the usual path. The Qur'an says something similar about fasting in 2:185: God wants ease for you, not hardship.

And a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari reports the Prophet ﷺ saying the religion is ease, and no one makes it too hard for himself without being overwhelmed by it. So aim close to the mark, he said, and take heart.
None of this means nothing is asked. The prayers are still prayed; the fast is still kept. But in the verse's picture, the asking comes from the One who knows the size of the one being asked.
It echoes al-Baqarah's last verse: wus'a, not beyond what you can bear.

how: Islamic law builds in concessions (rukhsa) for weakness, such as shortening prayers when traveling, praying seated when ill, and making up missed fasts, and Muslim teachers cite 4:28 and the hadith 'the religion is ease' when encouraging steady, moderate practice.

o: created weak by design, so the load is made light
too weak to be asked for anything at all
weak because people chose to give in to desire

p: God would make the burden light

s: it says they were created weak, and so the burden is made light.
the verse comes in a passage about marriage law
4:25–28 include allowances for those who can't manage the usual path.
light burden means nothing is asked
prayer and fasting remain; the asking is sized to the one asked.

games.q: a friend keeps adding extra worship until they burn out and stop altogether. what did the Prophet say about this, in Bukhari?
o: the religion is ease; no one overburdens himself without being overwhelmed.
stop entirely and start again next year.
games.why: aim close to the mark and take heart. steady and moderate, rather than heroic and short-lived.

practice: Think of one place you've been hard on yourself lately: a habit not broken, a missed goal, a skipped prayer.

Hear the voice you've been using, then try the verse's voice instead: you were made weak, and the load is meant to be light. Ask what a smaller, steadier, still faithful version of that goal would look like.
